title: Runtime contract registry
description: Objective: define the versioned command/query envelopes, lifecycle enums, nextAllowedCommands shape, and closed ErrorRegistry required by later application services. Deliverable: focused modules under packages/contracts/src/runtime with public package exports. NOT in scope: applying commands, persistence, HTTP, UI, or provider behavior. Hard dependencies: none. Owned paths: packages/contracts/src/runtime/** and packages/contracts/src/index.ts. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/contracts typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test.
definitionOfDone: Command/query envelopes are versioned, bounded, immutable, and reject unknown fields or versions.
Lifecycle enums and nextAllowedCommands are closed; unknown state or error grants no mutation affordance.
Every stable error maps to truth, retryability, and an exact recovery category without leaking input bytes.
The focused contracts typecheck and test command exits 0.
taskRails: Follow the pinned design; this task cannot create authority beyond its named contract.
Fail closed with stable codes and immutable deterministic outputs.
Keep production modules focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400.
Use TDD and stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, or merge.

implementationPlan.description: Create the closed runtime model and affordance vocabulary. Define frozen tuple-derived unions for the canonical TruthClass plus Project, Goal and scheduling control, GraphRevision, PlanningRun and drain overlay, NodeRun, Attempt, Lease, Effect, Integration, Approval state/decision/validity, QualificationRecovery, PlanningHold, supersession funding/fence, provider-slot, and Cutover states from design sections 6/8/12/16. Ratify the section-17 surface into disjoint operation tuples: queries are exactly `project.get`, `goal.get`, `goal.list`, `graph.get`, `graph.preview`, `dependency.explain`, `frontier.get`, `scheduler.readiness_explain`, `work.get_context`, `budget.get`, `evidence.get`, `quarantine.get`, `reconciliation.get`, `events.read`, `events.wait`, and `doctor.get`; `presence.ping` is telemetry and not a mutation affordance; every other listed v1 operation is a command. Define `NextAllowedCommand` as `{commandKind, commandId, commandEnvelopeVersion, inputSchemaVersion, targetAggregateId, expectedVersion, leaseAuthority?, graphRevisionHash?, policyRevisionHash?}` and a fresh-versus-historical result union. Implement a pure builder that accepts a tagged known lifecycle source, rejects malformed/unknown entries without partial authority, permits command kinds only, rejects duplicate command IDs, sorts by commandKind then commandId, deeply freezes the result, and returns the shared frozen empty array for any unknown source state. Keep the module <=250 lines.
implementationPlan.note: GREEN for the vocabulary/affordance suite: 8 passed, 1 failed (the strip-types smoke, which still needs step 3/4 exports). Closed 21 lifecycle tuples from design 6/8/12/16 (PROJECT, GOAL, GOAL_SCHEDULING, GRAPH_REVISION, PLANNING_RUN incl. SUBMISSION_DRAINING overlay, NODE_RUN, ATTEMPT, LEASE, EFFECT, INTEGRATION, APPROVAL/_DECISION/_VALIDITY, QUALIFICATION_RECOVERY, PLANNING_HOLD/_KIND, SUPERSESSION_FUNDING, PLANNING_FENCE, PROVIDER_SLOT, CUTOVER, TRUTH_CLASS). Ratified section 17 into disjoint tuples: 16 queries, 1 telemetry (presence.ping), 92 commands. Builder rejects unknown source/state, non-arrays, malformed entries, duplicate command IDs, and query/telemetry kinds; sorts by commandKind then commandId on code units (no locale); deep-freezes; returns the shared EMPTY_NEXT_ALLOWED_COMMANDS identity for every refusal. SCOPE NOTE: the plan asked for one module <=250 lines; the combined vocabulary+guards+builder came to 321 physical lines, so it was split into three focused modules under the owned path (runtime-guards.ts 76, runtime-vocabulary.ts 140, runtime-affordance.ts 137) with one-line .js strip-types bridges each. This raises the bridge count from the plan's three to (eventually) five; the <=250 rail takes precedence.

implementationPlan.description: Create the closed versioned ErrorRegistry. Define the stable codes `INPUT_INVALID`, `INPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED`, `AUTHENTICATION_FAILED`, `CAPABILITY_DENIED`, `SESSION_EXPIRED`, `SESSION_REPLAYED`, `STALE_LEASE`, `STALE_EPOCH`, `EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT`, `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`, `ILLEGAL_TRANSITION`, `HARD_DEPENDENCY_UNPROVEN`, `DEPENDENCY_REDUNDANT`, `FRONTIER_STALLED`, `FANOUT_SCOPE_REFUSED`, `FANOUT_ORACLE_REFUSED`, `FANOUT_BUDGET_REFUSED`, `FANOUT_FLOW_REFUSED`, `PLANNING_SUBMISSION_FINALIZING`, `SUPERSESSION_PREPARED`, `PLANNING_DISPOSITION_UNKNOWN`, `SUPERSESSION_CONSEQUENCE_CHANGED`, `SUPERSEDED_AUTHORITY`, `REVISION_REBOUND`, `PROVIDER_CAPABILITY_CHANGED`, `METERING_UNAVAILABLE`, `INTEGRATION_PROVENANCE_INVALID`, `INPUT_PROVENANCE_INVALID`, `JOURNAL_LIMIT_REACHED`, `CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE`, `STORAGE_DEGRADED`, `DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH`, `RESTORE_REQUIRED`, `CUTOVER_STATE_INVALID`, `NEEDS_RECONCILIATION`, `OUT_OF_SCOPE_HOST_EFFECT_UNKNOWN`, and `UNKNOWN_ERROR`. For every code, provide one frozen exhaustive descriptor with TruthClass, retryability (`NEVER|AFTER_REFRESH|AFTER_FACT_CHANGE|AFTER_RECOVERY`), recovery category (`NONE|CORRECT_REQUEST|REAUTHENTICATE|REFRESH|WAIT_OR_OBSERVE|REPLAN|RECONCILE|HUMAN_DECISION|INSPECT_OR_EXPORT|CANCEL`), exact recovery operation tuple, HTTP/MCP transport category/status/code, exact valid lifecycle sources, and an allowlist of required safe scalar detail keys. Implement exhaustive lookup/error construction: known codes copy only allowlisted scalar details into a frozen null-prototype record; missing required details are omitted rather than guessed; unknown code or unknown source resolves to `UNKNOWN_ERROR`, TruthClass UNKNOWN, no details, and the shared frozen empty recovery/affordance set while retaining only a validated correlation ID. Keep the registry <=250 lines.
implementationPlan.note: GREEN for the registry suite: 3 passed (exhaustive frozen descriptors, detail sanitization, unknown-code/source degradation); the 4th test in that describe block needs step 4's decoder. All 38 stable codes are mapped to one frozen descriptor with TruthClass, retryability, recovery category, exact recovery command tuple, transport category/httpStatus/mcpCode, exact valid lifecycle sources, and an allowlisted required-detail key set. Boundary codes (INPUT_INVALID, INPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED, AUTHENTICATION_FAILED, CAPABILITY_DENIED, SESSION_*) declare zero valid sources and must be raised without one; every other code requires a known lifecycle source whose aggregate is listed, else it degrades. Sanitization is double-gated: per-code key allowlist plus a bounded safe-scalar value check (`/^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}$/`, safe integers, booleans), copied into a frozen null-prototype record, so payload/credential/token/digest/stack/SQL can never ride through even under an allowlisted key. There is deliberately no `message` field, removing the last echo channel. SCOPE NOTE: the single registry module came to 284 physical lines, so the table (runtime-error-registry.ts, 188) and the construction/sanitization path (runtime-error-factory.ts, 104) were split into two focused modules with one-line .js bridges each.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the byte ingress decoders by composing `decodeBoundedJsonBytes`, preserving its exact 1 MiB/depth-64/string-256-KiB N/N+1 behavior and immutable snapshot semantics. `decodeRuntimeCommandEnvelopeBytes` must accept only `{schemaVersion, commandKind, commandId, correlationId, requestDigest, sessionCredential, targetAggregateId, expectedVersion, leaseAuthority?, graphRevisionHash?, policyRevisionHash?, payload}` where `leaseAuthority`, when present, has exactly `{leaseToken, epoch, authorityHash, graphEpoch, attemptBindingVersion}`; require nonempty strings, lowercase 64-hex digests/hashes, safe nonnegative integer versions/epochs, a plain JSON-object payload, a closed command kind, all-or-none lease fields, and no unknown/symbol/accessor keys. `decodeRuntimeQueryEnvelopeBytes` must accept only `{schemaVersion, queryKind, correlationId, sessionCredential, targetAggregateId?, cursor?, payload}`, use the exact closed query tuple, and reject mutation-only version/lease/revision/command fields. Validate in deterministic order: decoded record, schemaVersion, exact key set, kind, identifiers/digests, numeric bindings, then payload. Map body/depth/string limit errors to `INPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, unsupported versions to `SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED`, and all other syntax/shape failures to `INPUT_INVALID`; construct errors through the registry so no attacker bytes or secrets are reflected. Return only deeply frozen discriminated results and keep the module <=250 lines.
implementationPlan.note: GREEN: `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts typecheck` clean and `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test` = 6 files / 92 tests passed. runtime-envelope.ts (212 lines) composes decodeBoundedJsonBytes first, so the existing 1 MiB body / depth 64 / 256 KiB string / duplicate-key / interoperable-number rules and the immutable snapshot apply before any schema inspection. Validation order is exactly: decoded plain record, schemaVersion, exact key set, kind, identifiers/digests, numeric bindings (expectedVersion then all-or-none leaseAuthority), payload. Command envelope accepts only the 9 required + 3 optional keys; query envelope only 5 required + cursor/targetAggregateId, and rejects expectedVersion/leaseAuthority/graph+policyRevisionHash/commandKind/commandId/requestDigest as unknown keys. Limit codes map to INPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with safe {limitName, limitBytes}, version mismatch to SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED, everything else to INPUT_INVALID; every error is built through createRuntimeError so nothing from the input bytes is reflected. Results and envelopes are frozen and payloads stay deeply frozen from the decoder. Also fixed a real typecheck defect found here: inline Object.freeze([...]) in the registry table widened to readonly string[] and silently defeated literal checking of recovery command/source/detail keys; replaced with typed cmds()/srcs()/keys() helpers so every table cell is now literal-checked against the closed vocabularies.

implementationPlan.note: REAL DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED (fail-closed rail violation): `isPlainRecord` called `Array.isArray(value)` before `types.isProxy(value)`, and `Array.isArray` THROWS `TypeError: Cannot perform 'IsArray' on a proxy that has been revoked`. So a revoked proxy passed to createRuntimeError (as input, details, or source), buildNextAllowedCommands (as source, entries, or an entry), or freshRuntimeResult escaped as an uncaught exception instead of failing closed - violating the epic rail and the repo's existing hostile-input convention (control-room-model already asserts `.not.toThrow()` on revoked proxies). Fixed via TDD: added red tests in both files (confirmed failing with that exact TypeError), then moved the proxy check ahead of Array.isArray and added `isSafeArray` for the entries array. Re-probed all 9 public entry points with revoked object and callable proxies: all fail closed. Also cleaned two smells: createRuntimeError called isPlainRecord twice (once purely for narrowing), and the command decoder placed the unvalidated expectedVersion into the draft before isSafeCount ran (no leak, since every failure path returned before freeze, but the ordering was fragile) - now assigned only after validation. ADVERSARIAL PROBE (all clean): JSON duplicate keys; __proto__/constructor/prototype keys rejected with no global pollution; raw numeric literals -0, 9007199254740992, 1e-3, 2e308 all INPUT_INVALID while 0/1.0/1e3/1E2 correctly normalize; frozen against mutation of envelope, nested lease, and deep payload arrays; byte-identical repeat output; all 92 command kinds rejected by the query decoder and all 16 query kinds rejected by the command decoder; all 16 queries + presence.ping return the shared EMPTY set from the affordance builder while all 92 commands are admissible; affordance array resists push; secret injection ({payload, sessionCredential, leaseToken, requestDigest, stack, sql, ${...}, <script>, 999-char value}) attempted against EVERY code x EVERY valid source with zero leakage and EMPTY affordances everywhere. VOCABULARY CROSS-CHECK: parsed section 17 lines 986-1005 of the pinned design and diffed against the contracts - 109 operations parsed, 109 in contracts, zero missing and zero extra. LINE_COUNT_GATE PASS (cross-platform Node, CRLF/LF-safe): index.ts 114, all runtime/*.ts <=250 (max 250), all 6 bridges exactly 1 line. DIFF SCOPE: only `packages/contracts/src/index.ts` (M) and `packages/contracts/src/runtime/**` (untracked); no scratch or generated evidence files; authoritative design doc untouched. planningNotes.approachesConsidered: A single runtime registry file was rejected because it would mix wire parsing, lifecycle/affordance vocabulary, and error policy and would violate the user's no-large-files rail. The plan uses three focused TypeScript modules plus the repository-required one-line .js strip-types bridges. A separate schema generator is out of scope for this slice. The design does not pin common query fields or version literals, so this plan explicitly chooses minimal fail-closed v1 shapes rather than leaving those choices to the worker.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: The @moe/contracts package is root-export-only and uses explicit .js specifiers backed by tracked one-line `export * from "./name.ts"` bridges. Existing decodeBoundedJsonBytes already snapshots hostile byte inputs, enforces 1,048,576-byte bodies, depth 64, and 262,144-byte UTF-8 strings, rejects duplicate keys/non-interoperable numbers, and deeply freezes decoded JSON. Runtime envelope parsing must compose after it, not duplicate or relax it. Existing store request identity uses `moe-command-request/1`, expectedVersion, commandKind, targetAggregateId, correlationId, and historical `requiresAffordanceRefresh`; runtime contracts must preserve the rule that historical replay carries no current affordances.
planningNotes.risks: The authoritative design intentionally leaves the common query envelope, nextAllowedCommands JSON shape, retry/recovery enums, and version literals unspecified. Use the exact decisions in the steps below. Never reflect payload, credential, lease token, request bytes/digest, stack, SQL, or arbitrary attacker detail into errors. Unknown operation/state/error/version must fail closed and expose no mutation affordance. Keep every touched production or test source at or below 250 physical lines; use compact table-driven data/tests rather than weakening coverage.
